result:
The proposed answer of 7 appears to be wrong, though I am relying on recall of the literature rather than a derivation.

The relevant result, as I remember it, is from the paper on cuts in graphs with matching conflicts. It states that every simple connected planar 4-regular graph has a conflict-free cut for any 1-regular conflict graph, except for one graph. I believe that exception is the octahedron, which has 6 vertices.

The octahedron is plausible as the exception because a 1-regular conflict graph pairs up its 12 edges into 6 conflicting pairs. For the 4 edges at a vertex to form a conflict-free cut, no two of them may be paired. A suitable pairing can make every cut fail. Larger planar 4-regular graphs have more room to avoid such a blocking pairing.

The proposed solution gives no derivation. It simply asserts that the graph has 7 vertices, so nothing in it supports that number.

VERDICT: REJECT
